plant_name: Narada Jiuquan storage cell base (Jiuquan Narada Smart Energy Storage Manufacturing Base)
parent_company: Zhejiang Narada Power Source Co., Ltd.
research_notes: Located in Jiuquan Economic Development Zone, Gansu Province, China. Operated by Jiuquan Narada (酒泉南都), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Narada Power; not a JV. Total investment ~2bn yuan (RMB), ~200 mu (~13.3 ha) site. Gansu's first LFP energy-storage battery + system-integration project. Strategic cooperation agreement signed July 2023, land acquired Aug 2023, construction from Sept 2023; production launch ceremony held 18 June 2024, so status = operational. Phase 1 nameplate is 4 GWh/year of LFP lithium battery CELLS (电芯 production line confirmed by multiple Chinese trade sources — desn.com.cn, itdcw.com, Gansu Daily), plus co-located PACK and energy-storage system integration; qualifies as a cell manufacturer. End market is stationary energy storage (ESS). Cell_format set to prismatic as strong inference for large-format LFP storage cells (not explicitly stated in sources). Exact plant coordinates not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null (Jiuquan city is ~39.7N, 98.5E for reference only). Capacity figure is the phase-1 4 GWh nameplate for 2024; no phased ramp schedule published, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Cross-checked: Narada 2024/2025 filings describe total lithium cell capacity ~10 GWh with 4 GWh Jiuquan line built during H1 2024, consistent with this site being the 4 GWh addition.

plant_name: Envision AESC Yichang storage super factory
research_notes: Located in Yichang High-tech Zone, Hubei province, China. Envision AESC's dedicated energy-storage cell base, described as the world's first 100 GWh-level energy-storage full-industry-chain base (electrode, cell, pack). Phase 1 (40 GWh cell capacity; total investment ~CNY 12bn) began construction Oct 2025 and was put into operation 15 July 2026, rolling off the industry's largest 790Ah prismatic wound ESS cell (>2.5 kWh, >440 Wh/L, >12,000 cycles), first batch shipped to Germany. Phase 2 (60 GWh cells + 60 GWh AI energy-storage systems) broke ground April 2026, targeted operational 2027, bringing the site to 100 GWh cell + 60 GWh system capacity. Total site investment ~CNY 24.2bn. Status set operational because Phase 1 is producing; Phase 2 is under construction. nameplate_capacity_gwh=100 is the eventual full cell nameplate (system capacity excluded as this table tracks cell output). Chemistry LFP inferred from large-format long-cycle ESS cell spec (not explicitly stated in sources). Coordinates not sourced, left null. Cross-checked across EnergyTrend (EN) and Sina/Eastmoney/CLS/STDaily (CN) trade press; Nissan legacy Zama/other Envision AESC EV sites are separate.

plant_name: Trina Storage Chuzhou LFP cell gigafactory
research_notes: LOCATION CORRECTION: The candidate name says "Changzhou" (Trina Solar's corporate HQ in Jiangsu), but Trina Storage's actual LFP battery CELL gigafactory is in Chuzhou, Anhui Province. This is the intended site. Trina Storage is the energy-storage subsidiary of Trina Solar. It announced vertical integration and an LFP cell gigafactory in May 2022 (alongside the Elementa cabinet launch). It completed 12 GWh of energy-storage battery capacity (cells + PACK modules + system integration) at its Chuzhou base in 2023 — hence status = operational, nameplate 12 GWh/yr (ref 2023). The site makes battery cells (confirmed cell manufacturer), so is_cell_manufacturer = true. Chemistry is LFP; products are large-format prismatic ESS cells (e.g. 306Ah/314Ah, earlier 587Ah), so cell_format = prismatic (inferred from product line, moderate confidence) and end_market = ESS. EXPANSION (announced, not counted in nameplate): In March 2026 an RMB 7.2bn "36 GWh Lithium Battery and R&D Center" project in Chuzhou was added to Anhui's 2026 Key Project List, with an EIA submitted — 36 GWh of mass-production cell capacity plus a 1 GWh pilot line. Sources indicate the Chuzhou base would reach ~48 GWh total once the expansion is complete. Because that expansion is at announced/EIA stage (not operational), nameplate is kept at the confirmed operational 12 GWh rather than summing across statuses. Trina Storage also operates a separate facility in Yancheng, Jiangsu (distinct site). Coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Not a JV — wholly Trina Storage/Trina Solar. Other sources: Trina Solar newsroom (May 2022 LFP cell gigafactory announcement), energy-storage.news, pv-magazine.

CATL's first battery cell plant outside China, at the Erfurter Kreuz industrial park in Amt Wachsenburg (Arnstadt area), Thuringia, south of Erfurt — commonly referred to as "CATL Erfurt" or "CATL Arnstadt". Serial lithium-ion cell production began December 2022; official opening early 2023 (electrive/Exyte/invest-in-thuringia). Total investment ~EUR 1.8bn, ~1,700-2,000 jobs. Nameplate design capacity 14 GWh/yr (initial line ~8 GWh, ramping to 14 GWh); some German press (electrive) report a planned gradual expansion to 24 GWh to supply BMW and Mercedes — treated as a plan, not current nameplate, so recorded 14 GWh. Cells are prismatic NMC for EV automakers (BMW, which holds a CATL stake and placed a EUR 7.3bn order; also Mercedes). Chemistry (NMC) and prismatic format inferred from CATL's European automotive product line rather than an explicit plant-level statement — hence confidence 0.8. Coordinates are approximate for the Erfurter Kreuz CATL site (not from an official geocoded source). Note: separate, larger ~50 GWh "Erfurt/Thuringia phase 2" expansion reported under construction with production targeted ~late 2026 — a distinct future project, not counted here. capacity_by_year_json reflects the 8→14 GWh ramp.

Battery cell gigafactory in Heide, Dithmarschen district, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany (near the municipalities of Lohe-Rickelshof and Norderwöhrden). Announced by Northvolt in March 2022; site formally committed January 2024; groundbreaking/start of construction March 2024 (attended by Chancellor Scholz). Northvolt's original design was a full nameplate of 60 GWh/yr (enough for ~800k-1m EVs), targeting first production in 2026 and full ramp by 2029, using NMC prismatic cells for the EV market, powered by regional wind.

Northvolt AB filed for bankruptcy (Sweden, March 2025). Construction in Heide stalled with only site preparation done, but was officially kept alive. US firm Lyten (lithium-sulfur specialist) agreed to acquire the Heide site; it completed acquisition of Northvolt's Swedish units in Feb 2026 and agreed a ~EUR 60m purchase of the Heide site (federal government/state/KfW) reported June 2026. The Schleswig-Holstein LfU issued the first partial BImSchG permit for the Heide plant in April 2026, and Lyten/Northvolt began repaying state funding.

Lyten has scaled the site down from Northvolt's plans: ~15 GWh currently under construction with a path to 30+ GWh (vs Northvolt's 60 GWh), and ~1,000 jobs (vs 3,000). Lyten intends NMC lithium-ion cells initially with lithium-sulfur to follow. nameplate_capacity_gwh recorded as Northvolt's original 60 GWh full design (capacity_ref_year 2029); note the realistic near-term nameplate under Lyten is ~15 GWh. start_year left null given repeated delays and ownership change. Coordinates left null (no precisely sourced lat/long for the exact site; it lies just west of Heide town at roughly 54.2N, 9.05E - not sourced, so null). Confidence moderate: plant existence, location, chemistry and format well documented, but capacity, status timeline and ownership are in flux. Corroborating sources: pv-magazine (2024-03-27, 60 GWh groundbreaking), Northvolt.com articles, electrive (2025-10-09 Lyten plans; 2026-04-10 partial permit; 2026-06-22 EUR60m purchase), Lyten press releases (Feb 2026), electriccarsreport (Feb 2026).

PowerCo SE (Volkswagen Group battery subsidiary) commissioned the Salzgitter gigafactory and produced the first "Unified Cells" made in Europe on 17 December 2025; status therefore operational, with production ramping through 2026. Foundation stone laid July 2022 (announced). First-step annual nameplate capacity is up to 20 GWh, expandable to up to 40 GWh "if required" (not yet committed) — hence nameplate recorded as 20 GWh; 40 GWh is a conditional future expansion, not a fixed phased ramp, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Product is the prismatic PowerCo Unified Cell based on NMC chemistry (standardised format designed to accommodate other chemistries including future solid-state); dimensions 256 x 24.8 x 106 mm. End market is EV (VW Group volume models; cells shipped e.g. to Martorell for cell-to-pack). Salzgitter is the lead plant for sister PowerCo gigafactories in Valencia (Spain) and St. Thomas (Canada). Coordinates are the VW Salzgitter component plant site (approximate, city/plant-level, not independently source-confirmed to the exact cell building). Sources: Volkswagen Group press release and electrive/eeNews/Automotive Logistics coverage of the 17 Dec 2025 production start, and electrive July 2022 groundbreaking coverage.

Single physical site at Grünheide (Mark), Brandenburg, ~35 km SE of Berlin; primarily a Model Y vehicle assembly plant that is now adding an in-house 4680 cylindrical cell manufacturing line (cell production, not just pack assembly). History: original cell plans (up to 100 GWh, later floated to 250 GWh) were put on hold in 2022 as Tesla prioritised the US. Cell manufacturing was revived in December 2025 with an 8 GWh/yr target for 2027; in May 2026 Tesla raised the target to 18 GWh/yr with an additional ~$250M investment (cumulative site cell spend reported ~$1.2–1.45bn, >1,500 planned cell jobs). Multiple sources report Giga Berlin officially began producing initial 4680 cells on 12 May 2026, but this is early/ramp-up production; commercial full-scale 4680 cell production is targeted for H1 2027 — hence status recorded as under_construction and nameplate_capacity_gwh=18 referenced to 2027. Marked start_year=2027 for commercial production (first pilot cells produced May 2026). Chemistry is Tesla's 4680 cylindrical cell, high-nickel NMC (reported NMC 811 shifting toward NMC 955), produced via Tesla's dry battery electrode (DBE) process. Not a JV — wholly Tesla-operated. Coordinates approximate (~52.396N, 13.789E). No clearly sourced year-by-year GWh ramp schedule found, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Corroborating sources: electrive (2025-12-17, 2026-05-13), Electrek (2026-05-12), autoevolution, teslanorth (2026-07-06).

parent_company: Automotive Cells Company (JV of Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz, TotalEnergies/Saft)
chemistry: NMC (lithium-ion); LFP was under consideration before cancellation
research_notes: CANCELLED PROJECT — never built. ACC's planned battery cell + module gigafactory on a ~34 ha site adjacent to the Opel components plant in western Kaiserslautern. Announced ~2021; received a €437m German IPCEI grant (Sept 2021, total public support ~€450m) toward ~€2bn investment. Production of cells/modules was planned to begin end-2025 at an initial ~13.4 GWh/yr, scaling to 40 GWh/yr (enough for 600,000+ EVs). Construction was put on standby in May/June 2024 amid weak European EV demand, high energy/materials/build costs, and a possible pivot from NMC lithium-ion to LFP. In early February 2026 ACC informed unions the Kaiserslautern (and Italian Termoli) projects were definitively shelved/cancelled. It therefore never reached under_construction of the cell lines nor operation; 'announced' is the closest schema status but the project is effectively dead. ACC is owned by Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and TotalEnergies (via Saft); its only operational plant is Billy-Berclau/Douvrin, France. Chemistry/format based on ACC's NMC pouch-cell technology at Douvrin. Capacity figures are the original PLANNED nameplate/ramp, never realised. Coordinates left null (not sourced with confidence). Corroborated by CNBC, Euronews, Automotive Manufacturing Solutions and German trade press (Feb 2026).

Cellforce Group GmbH, based in Kirchentellinsfurt near Reutlingen/Tuebingen, Germany. Founded 2021 as a JV between Porsche AG and CUSTOMCELLS; Porsche took full ownership in June 2023, so it is now a Porsche subsidiary (jv_partners kept for history). Foundation stone laid Oct 2022; designed as a "ramp-up" factory with annual capacity of at least ~1 GWh/yr (initial cell manufacturing of high-performance cells for ~up to 200,000 hp EVs was the later 20 GWh aspiration). Chemistry: BASF HED NCM cathode with silicon anode (silicon material from Group14); cells are lithium-ion pouch format for high-performance automotive (EV) applications. 

CRITICAL STATUS NOTE: In August 2025 Porsche scrapped the plan to expand to high-volume/mass cell production at Cellforce, citing slower EV ramp and market conditions in China/USA. ~200 of 286 staff at the Kirchentellinsfurt site faced layoffs. The site is being retained only as an independent R&D unit with a PILOT production line (for know-how transfer and next-generation chemistry / battery-system development). So the ~1 GWh ramp-up nameplate and the earlier 20 GWh expansion are effectively cancelled; only pilot-scale cell production remains. Status marked 'operational' because a pilot cell line is running, but commercial gigawatt-scale production will not proceed. nameplate_capacity_gwh (1 GWh) reflects the original ramp-up-factory design figure, not confirmed realised output — treat with low confidence given the 2025 cancellation. start_year 2024 (approx. planned production start) is inferred. Coordinates are town-level for Kirchentellinsfurt, not a confirmed exact factory location. 

Sources: Porsche Newsroom (25 Aug 2025) refocus on R&D; electrive.com (18 Aug 2025 cuts, 25 Aug 2025 halt; 19 Oct 2022 capacity expansion; 16 Jun 2023 Porsche takeover/20 GWh); Battery-News.de (26 Aug 2025); evertiq.com. Cross-checked: capacity figures conflict across years (1 GWh ramp-up vs 20 GWh aspiration) and 2025 news confirms mass production abandoned.

Verkor's first gigafactory, located in Bourbourg on the Grand Port Maritime de Dunkerque industrial zone (address: 7264 route du cap horn, 59630 Bourbourg). Site selected Feb 2022; foundation stone/construction Nov 2023; officially inaugurated and production begun 11 December 2025. Initial nameplate capacity 16 GWh/year (ramp target 2026), planned expansion to 50 GWh by 2030 - nameplate_capacity_gwh set to the eventual 50 GWh (ref year 2030) per phased-ramp rule; capacity_by_year_json captures the 16 GWh (2026) to 50 GWh (2030) ramp. Chemistry is low-carbon NMC lithium-ion; primary product is large pouch cells (Verkor's broader range also includes cylindrical). First cells destined for the Alpine A390 EV (Renault Group) from 2026 - end market EV. Not a JV: Verkor is an independent French company (investors/customers include Renault Group, Macquarie, EQT, Sibanye-Stillwater), so operator and parent set to Verkor and jv_partners left null. ~1,200 direct jobs. Coordinates left null - no precisely sourced lat/long found (Bourbourg town centre is ~50.94N, 2.20E but the plant sits on the port ZGI to the north). Cross-checked across electrive, Verkor press release, Batteries News and battery-news.de. Confirmed cell manufacturer.

parent_company: Automotive Cells Company (JV of Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and TotalEnergies/Saft)
research_notes: Site located at Billy-Berclau/Douvrin, Hauts-de-France (former Française de Mécanique/PSA site). First large-scale European gigafactory of ACC, a JV owned by Stellantis (45%), Mercedes-Benz (30%) and TotalEnergies (25%). Inaugurated May 2023; production began end of 2023 with progressive 2024 ramp-up. Chemistry is NMC (lithium nickel cobalt manganese) pouch cells for EVs; ACC has stated it is revising strategy toward lower-cobalt/nickel and cost-effective chemistries (possible future LFP), but Douvrin's product to date is NMC pouch. As of early 2026 reporting, ACC has shelved its previously planned Kaiserslautern (Germany) and Termoli (Italy) gigafactories and is concentrating on ramping the French Douvrin site — those are separate physical sites and excluded here. Coordinates left null (not confirmed from a source). Announced_year set to 2020 (ACC JV founding / project launch). AESC (subsidiary of China's Envision Group) started production (SOP) at its Douai gigafactory in June 2025, with President Macron attending. It is a wholly AESC-owned cell + module plant (not a JV); Renault is the anchor customer, supplying NMC cells for the electric Renault 5 and other volume EVs. Phase 1 confirmed operational nameplate ~10 GWh/yr; planned expansion via further phases to 24-30 GWh/yr by 2030 (Renault confirmed 24 GWh; other sources cite up to 30 GWh). European auto-market slowdown may delay the 2030 expansion. Total initial investment ~EUR 1.3bn (earlier figures cited up to EUR 2bn incl. expansion). Located in Douai, Hauts-de-France, adjacent to Renault's Georges Besse / ElectriCity site. The plant runs the full chain: electrode from powders, cell manufacture, and module assembly, so it qualifies as a genuine cell manufacturer. Cell format recorded as pouch (AESC's traditional laminated pouch design) with moderate confidence; not explicitly confirmed in the fetched sources. Coordinates left null (not sourced). Capacity figures cross-checked across electrive, Nord France Invest, and Renault Group media. source_date reflects access date. Additional sources: https://www.nordfranceinvest.com/news/automotive-sector-envision-aesc-to-build-the-hauts-de-france-regions-second-gigafactory/ ; https://media.renaultgroup.com/renault-group-places-france-at-the-heart-of-its-industrial-strategy-for-ev-batteries/

Wholly owned CATL site (not a JV) in the Southern Industrial Zone of Debrecen, Hungary. Investment c. €7.3 billion. Announced August 2022 as Europe's largest planned battery cell gigafactory. Phase 1 nameplate 40 GWh/year; full/eventual nameplate 100 GWh/year (no firm year for the 100 GWh stage, so capacity_ref_year left null). nameplate_capacity_gwh set to the eventual 100 GWh; capacity_by_year_json shows the 40 GWh phase-1 step nominally targeted for 2026.

Status: classified under_construction as of July 2026. The plant building and cell lines are complete and phase-1 capacity (40 GWh) is reported fully booked, but serial CELL production had NOT yet started (repeatedly delayed from the planned March/April 2026 start, pending permits). A separate 5 GWh module/pack assembly line began production in June 2026 - but module assembly is not cell manufacturing. Mercedes-Benz was reported (June 2026) sourcing cells from China because Debrecen cell output had not begun. Once cell serial production starts, status should move to operational.

Chemistry: primarily NMC prismatic cells for European automakers; also reported to supply P6 prismatic NCA cells for Hyundai's European EVs from 2026, and some cylindrical output cited - hence mixed leaning NMC. Cell format recorded as prismatic (dominant); some cylindrical also reported.

End market: EV. Confirmed/likely customers include BMW (builds iX3 nearby), Mercedes-Benz/Daimler, Stellantis, Volkswagen, Hyundai.

Coordinates left null - not confirmed to sufficient precision from a source; site is in Debrecen's Southern Industrial Park.

Confidence 0.8: capacity, status, timeline and ownership well covered by multiple reputable outlets (electrive, Reuters-cited news, Xinhua, CnEVPost, CEENergyNews); exact chemistry split and precise coordinates less certain.

Additional sources: https://cnevpost.com/2025/09/08/catl-hungarian-plant-begin-production-early-2026/ ; https://www.electrive.com/2026/06/23/catl-sources-battery-components-from-china-instead-of-debrecen/ ; https://insideevs.com/news/604099/catl-100gwh-battery-plant-hungary/ ; https://english.news.cn/europe/20251204/2fa573891f854f7388a31fb88d34b6f6/c.html

chemistry: NCA (high-nickel, prismatic; P6 stacked cells ~91% Ni with silicon anode)
research_notes: Wholly owned Samsung SDI plant in Göd (Göd Újtelep industrial zone, ~30 km north of Budapest), not a JV. Two production units built in phases: original investment decision ~2016, inauguration/first production 2017, second unit completed 2019 reaching full ramp by early 2022. Currently operational with combined annual capacity ~40 GWh (2025). Samsung SDI announced a ~€1bn renovation/expansion in 2025 (part of a ~1.65tn won capital raise; ~323.6bn won directly into the facility) converting the first factory from wound to high-energy-density stacked prismatic cells and raising total capacity to ~60 GWh by 2026 — hence nameplate 60 GWh (ref 2026) with phased ramp in capacity_by_year_json. Produces prismatic PRiMX cells (both wound and stacked methods); from 2026 supplies Hyundai/Kia in Europe with 6th-gen P6 stacked prismatic NCA cells (~91% nickel, silicon-based anode) under a 2026–2032 contract. Also supplies BMW, Volkswagen and Stellantis. Chemistry is high-nickel NCA/NMC family; recorded as NCA-prismatic. Coordinates left null — no source gave exact plant lat/long (town of Göd only). Capacity figures corroborated across battery-news.de, electrive, CEENERGYNEWS and battery-tech.net; status and expansion well sourced, hence confidence 0.8.

SK On (part of SK Innovation / SK Group) runs two Li-ion battery CELL plants at Komarom, Hungary, treated here as one Komarom site. Komarom I: construction from Feb 2018, first production ~2019/2020, ~7.5 GWh/yr, five assembly lines, NCM 811 pouch cells for EV. Komarom II: commissioned 2022, initial ~9.8 GWh, scalable toward ~16 GWh; combined nameplate reported at ~17 GWh (7 + 10). Both plants are cell (and module) manufacturing for EV; reported running in the mid-80% utilisation range (Businesskorea). SK On also has a third, much larger Hungarian site at Ivancsa (~30 GWh) which is a separate physical location and NOT included in this Komarom row. nameplate_capacity_gwh = 17 is the combined operational annual capacity of the two Komarom plants; capacity_by_year_json shows the phased build (Plant 1 in 2020, Plant 2 added by 2022). Coordinates are town-level approximate for Komarom, Hungary (industrial park), not surveyed plant coordinates - lower confidence on lat/long specifically. Cross-checked across Businesskorea, battery-tech.net, electrive, thelec and SK On Hungary corporate site. source_date is access date (2026-07-19), not original publication date.

SK On's third and largest Hungarian battery cell plant, at Iváncsa (Fejér county, ~51 km SW of Budapest). Greenfield ~USD 2.29bn investment on a ~70-hectare site; announced Jan/Feb 2021. Mass production began in 2024 at 30 GWh/yr annual nameplate, reportedly reaching >90% yield within three months and lifting SK On's total European capacity to ~47.5 GWh (alongside the two Komárom plants). Not a JV — wholly owned by SK On (SK Innovation group). Cells are nickel-based NMC pouch cells for EVs (SK On specialises in NMC pouch; also developing mid-nickel variants). Site completion/ancillary works (road, rail connections) reportedly continuing to ~2028, but cell production is operational. Received EU/Hungary state aid (~EUR 209m reported). Customers include Hyundai, Kia, Ford, Volkswagen. Coordinates are the Iváncsa town centre (~47.083N, 18.75E) as an approximation — exact plant coordinates not confirmed from a primary source, so treat lat/long as low-precision. Capacity phasing beyond the 30 GWh full nameplate not separately sourced, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Cross-checked across electrive, Green Car Congress, HIPA, CEENERGYNEWS and battery-tech.net.

Largest EV battery cell factory in Europe, located in Biskupice Podgórne, Kobierzyce municipality, near Wrocław. Established 2016; mass production began ~2018. Current production capacity widely reported at 86 GWh/yr (2024), with a target of ~100 GWh/yr after a Stage IV expansion (and aspirations toward ~115 GWh). Historically NMC pouch cells for EVs (e.g. Volkswagen); LG has added LFP cell production for ESS/BESS (used in Polish PGE grid-scale projects), so end_market is mixed (EV + ESS). Cell format is pouch. Coordinates are approximate to the Biskupice Podgórne site (village/technology-park level, ~51.006N 16.955E) and not a company-confirmed plant centroid — treat with modest confidence. Capacity figures cross-checked across LG corporate pages, invest-in-wroclaw.pl, energy-storage.news, and trade press; 86 GWh (operational) vs 100 GWh (target) should not be blended. Sources: https://lgensol.pl/en/get-know-us/ , https://invest-in-wroclaw.pl/5-years-of-lg-energy-solution-wroclaw-the-largest-investment-in-the-region , https://www.energy-storage.news/pges-900mwh-bess-will-be-first-to-use-lgs-ess-batteries-produced-in-poland/

PowerCo's second gigafactory (after Salzgitter), in Sagunto/Parc Sagunt near Valencia, Spain, on ~130 ha. Wholly owned by Volkswagen Group via PowerCo — not a JV, so jv_partners null. Under construction as of 2025-2026; ~1,400 people working on site. Timeline slipped: series cell production now scheduled to begin July 2027 (previously targeted 2026), with a preseries/pilot phase Sept-Oct 2026. Will produce Volkswagen's prismatic "Unified Cell", which can run LFP or NMC chemistry (Valencia to start with LFP unified cells per multiple reports); hence chemistry recorded as mixed. Capacity: initial planned nameplate 40 GWh/year with potential expansion to 60 GWh (widely cited VW figure). Oct 2025 reporting states launch with two lines = 20 GWh, with the site designed for additional blocks up to 40 GWh; capacity_by_year_json therefore models 20 GWh at 2027 launch ramping toward the 40 GWh nameplate by ~2028 (ramp years inferred, the 20 GWh launch figure is sourced). Coordinates are approximate town/industrial-park level for Sagunto (Parc Sagunt), not a surveyed plant point. End market EV (Volkswagen Group EVs incl. Electric Urban Car Family / ID. Polo). Sources: electrive (2025-10-28), Volkswagen Group press releases, Battery-Tech Network, Green Car Congress / Battery Design on the Unified Cell.

50-50 JV between CATL and Stellantis to build an LFP battery cell (and module) gigafactory at Stellantis' existing Figueruelas site near Zaragoza, Spain. Total investment up to EUR 4.1bn. Groundbreaking / start of construction took place November 2025 (status = under_construction). Full nameplate capacity stated as "up to 50 GWh/year" (enough for ~1 million EVs), described as subject to the evolution of the European EV market and continued EU/Spanish government support. Chemistry confirmed LFP; end market EV. Timeline is CONFLICTING across sources: the original Dec 2024 announcement and several 2025 reports give production start "by end of 2026 / late 2026", while other groundbreaking-era reporting describes a phased build 2026-2030 with "cell and module production beginning in 2028." start_year set to 2026 (officially stated target) but treat as uncertain; capacity_ref_year 2030 reflects the phased ramp to full 50 GWh. No sourced year-by-year GWh ramp figures found, so capacity_by_year_json left null. Cell format not confirmed by a source (left null). Coordinates are for the adjacent Stellantis Figueruelas plant (the JV factory is on the same site). Sources: CATL official news (catl.com/en/news/6614.html and 6328.html), Stellantis press release (Dec 2024), and multiple trade outlets (electrive, automotivelogistics, mobilityportal, electriccarsreport).

plant_name: Envision AESC Navalmoral de la Mata (VENERGY+)
research_notes:
Battery cell gigafactory in the Espacio Navalmoral industrial park, Navalmoral de la Mata, Cáceres, Extremadura (part of Envision's planned Net Zero Industrial Park). Project branded VENERGY+. Groundbreaking ("first stone") ceremony held 8 July 2024 with Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez; 108 hectares reserved and site-preparation work initiated. Chemistry pivoted from the originally announced NMC to LFP (billed as one of Europe's first at-scale LFP producers). Phase-1 investment stated at >€1bn / ~$1.1bn, ~900 direct jobs.

CAPACITY IS CONFLICTING across sources: (a) headline announcements cite 30 GWh/yr phase-1 EV battery capacity, with some 2022 sources citing "up to 50 GWh phase 1" and others "10 GWh raised to 30 GWh by 2030"; (b) AESC Battery Spain's 2024 annual accounts (reported Aug 2025) describe a significant downscaling to two LFP lines totalling ~10.6 GWh/yr (from an earlier 3-line ~7.7 GWh NMC plan). I recorded nameplate_capacity_gwh=30 as the announced/eventual ambition, but the current realistic figure per the latest accounts is closer to ~10.6 GWh/yr — treat with caution.

STATUS/TIMING: heavily delayed and revised. Per the 2024 annual accounts, physical construction was planned to begin H2 2025 with operations ~March 2028 (earlier public claims of 2025/2026 production are outdated). A new environmental impact assessment was pending Extremadura regional approval as the 2023 declaration lapsed. Classified as under_construction given groundbreaking + site prep, but it may still be in late-permitting/early-works stage. start_year set to 2028 per latest guidance. Coordinates left null (specific site coords not sourced). cell_format not sourced. Not a site-level JV (AESC is an Envision Group company). Cross-checked: electrive, just-auto/Yahoo, miningsee, MarkLines, El Español, El Salto.

parent_company: Automotive Cells Company (JV of Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and TotalEnergies/Saft)
research_notes: ACC's planned third European gigafactory, on the brownfield Stellantis (ex-FCA) powertrain site at Termoli, Molise. Announced at Stellantis EV Day on 8 July 2021; targeted commissioning in 2026 ramping to up to 40 GWh/yr of NMC cells (~2,000 jobs by 2030). Never reached meaningful construction: work put on standby May/June 2024 amid weak EU EV demand; Italy withdrew its funding commitment in Sept 2024. In February 2026 ACC (Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz, TotalEnergies/Saft) officially SHELVED/ABANDONED the Termoli and Kaiserslautern projects — cited ~20-25% cost disadvantage vs Asian rivals and slow EV growth. Site never operated; project is effectively cancelled. Schema lacks a 'cancelled' status, so recorded as 'announced' (highest stage genuinely reached) — treat as dead/withdrawn. Capacity 40 GWh is the eventual full nameplate; no reliable phased ramp figures. Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null (site is the existing Stellantis Termoli plant). Corroborating sources: electrive.com (2026-02-09, permanent abandonment; 2024-06-05 hold; 2024-09-19 Italy funding withdrawal), CNBC/Reuters (2026-02-07), automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com (40 GWh figure).

Announced Feb 2021 as Italy's first large-scale Li-ion cell gigafactory, on the former Olivetti industrial site at Scarmagno (province of Turin), Piedmont. Planned nameplate ~45 GWh/year (some releases said up to 70 GWh long-term); NMC chemistry with planned silicon anodes and licensed StoreDot extreme-fast-charging tech; planned pouch/prismatic/cylindrical formats (hence cell_format=mixed); target markets EV + ESS (end_market=mixed). Original production target 2024, later slipped to 2025+. PROJECT EFFECTIVELY FAILED / NEVER BUILT: never progressed to actual construction of cell production. In Jan 2024 a Milan court opened crisis-management/liquidation proceedings (commissioner Antonino Ficalora) after the supervisory board sought liquidation and disputes with creditor/designer Pininfarina; site also hit suspected-asbestos and grid-connection problems. By ~April 2024 founder Lars Carlström publicly gave up on the Italian site and pivoted to a new UAE gigafactory (Statevolt Emirates, Ras Al Khaimah). Kept status='announced' because the schema has no 'cancelled' value and the plant never reached under_construction or operational; treat as a dead/abandoned announcement. Capacity 45 GWh is the never-realised planned nameplate, so capacity_ref_year and start_year left null. Coordinates are the approximate Scarmagno town location, not a confirmed exact plant footprint. is_cell_manufacturer=true by intended plant type (Li-ion cell manufacturing) though it never produced cells. Sources: battery-news.de (2024-01-19, danger of failing); electrive.com (2021-02-16, 45 GWh cell production); InsideEVs (ABB 45 GWh); bestmag.co.uk (2024, 'Italvolt gives up on Italy gigafactory, sets up in UAE').

Groundbreaking 6 July 2026 in Brindisi, Italy. JV between Eni Industrial Evolution and FIB (Seri Industrial Group) operating as Eni Storage Systems. Site produces LFP battery cells and modules plus a co-located BESS assembly plant; second phase adds LFP cathode active material production and recycling. Brindisi nameplate is 8 GWh/year; the wider hub targets 16 GWh/year by 2030 combined with Seri's Teverola plant (recorded only the 8 GWh Brindisi figure to avoid conflating two physical sites; the 16 GWh is cumulative across both). End market is stationary storage (BESS/ESS), stated as more than 10% of the European stationary storage market. No confirmed first-production year, phased annual ramp, cell format, or site coordinates found. Corroborated by ess-news.com and energy-storage.news (both 403 on direct fetch but summarised via search); Eni press release and multiple trade outlets align on 8 GWh Brindisi / 16 GWh hub and LFP cell+module production.

Northvolt Ett is Europe's first homegrown battery cell gigafactory, in Bergsbyn, Skellefteå, northern Sweden. First prismatic lithium-ion cell assembled 28 Dec 2021; site selection/announcement 2017. Designed/eventual full nameplate goal was ~60 GWh/yr (Ett plus Ett Expansion), but only ~16 GWh of cell production capacity was ever installed. Northvolt AB filed for bankruptcy in March 2025. US lithium-sulfur company Lyten agreed to acquire the Swedish assets (Northvolt Ett, Ett Expansion, and Northvolt Labs in Vasteras) in Aug 2025, completing the deal in Feb 2026 (~$5bn combined book value, 16 GWh existing cell capacity, 160+ ha land, plus Europe's largest battery R&D centre). Site is being operated by Lyten (as its first Industrial Hub), restarting production with commercial NMC cell shipments expected H2 2026, supplying Lyten's BESS assembly in Gdansk, Poland, plus automotive/mobility; Lyten also plans lithium-sulfur production and a data-centre development on site. Current cells are Li-ion NMC (prismatic). Status marked operational: plant is built and previously produced cells, now restarting under Lyten. Precise lat/long not confirmed from a citable source, left null. Capacity figures carry ambiguity (60 GWh design vs 16 GWh installed) hence confidence 0.8. Sources: Lyten press release 2026-02-26; Energy-Storage.News; just-auto/Yahoo Finance Aug 2025.

Europe's first GW-scale LFP gigafactory, located at Eyde Material Park in Arendal, Norway. Test/initial production began summer 2024; factory inaugurated 16 October 2024 by PM Jonas Gahr Store. Produces prismatic LFP cells; nameplate 1 GWh/yr (up to ~3 million cells/yr). Commercial start of production (SOP) declared January 2026; first commercial LFP cell shipments to Finland's Proventia began April 2026 under a supply agreement to 2031. The site physically manufactured and shipped cells, so status = operational for the built site. Morrow had planned to expand the Arendal site in four phases to a total 43 GWh (three additional ~14 GWh 'Eyde' modules), but this expansion NEVER materialised - do not treat 43 GWh as built/nameplate. Morrow Batteries ASA filed for bankruptcy in early May 2026 (board resolved 6 May 2026) after failing to secure investors; as of the source date no acquirer had been named and a bankruptcy administrator was being appointed by Agder District Court. Company also developed LNMO-X (high-voltage) technology. Coordinates and precise announced_year not confirmed by sources, left null. Sources: electrive (2026-05-11), Battery-News (2026-05-07), CleanTechnica (2024-08-22), MarkLines/mynewsdesk company releases.

New Sunderland gigafactory (often "AESC2") commenced operations 16 Dec 2025 at the International Advanced Manufacturing Park (IAMP), adjacent to Nissan Motor Manufacturing UK. Initial nameplate 15.8 GWh/yr (up from earlier 9 GWh 2021 / 12 GWh 2022 plans); supplies cells/modules for 200,000+ EVs/yr, principally Nissan. Lithium-ion NMC pouch cells. Now described as the UK's largest operational battery plant. Envision AESC is a subsidiary of China's Envision Group (majority owner; Nissan/others hold minority stakes) - treated as operator, not a JV site. The original co-located plant has produced cells since 2012 at ~1.9 GWh/yr. Expansion of the Sunderland campus up to ~35 GWh (and a discussed second/third UK gigafactory) has been mentioned but is not firmly committed, so nameplate kept at the confirmed 15.8 GWh. Precise lat/long not sourced (site is at IAMP, north-east of the Nissan plant near Sunderland, ~54.96N, -1.47W approx) - left null to avoid an unsourced coordinate. Corroborating: China Energy Storage Alliance (en.cnesa.org, 17 Dec 2025) and Sunderland City Council planning docs (lithium-ion pouch cells, NMC cathode).

plant_name: Agratas Somerset Gigafactory (Gravity Smart Campus, Bridgwater)
research_notes: Agratas (Tata Group's global battery business) is building the UK's largest battery cell gigafactory on the Gravity Smart Campus near Bridgwater, Somerset (former Royal Ordnance site, Puriton). ~£4bn investment, publicly confirmed for Somerset in February/March 2024. Nameplate 40 GWh/yr (~500,000 EVs/yr), expected to supply nearly half of UK automotive battery demand by the early 2030s. Anchor customers JLR and Tata Motors (end market EV). Chemistry: Agratas produces high-energy-density NMC and long-life LFP cells, so site is recorded as mixed. Status is under_construction as of 2026: ~16,800 piles installed, steel frame up, industrialisation started; construction is phased. Production timeline slipped from an initial 2026 target to late 2027 (grid infrastructure upgrades cited). On 9 April 2026 the UK government confirmed a £380m grant. Cell format not confirmed in sources (left null). No sourced site coordinates found, so lat/long left null (the Gravity/Puriton site location is publicly known but not confirmed via a cited source here). No published year-by-year capacity ramp, so capacity_by_year_json left null; 40 GWh is the eventual full nameplate reached in the early 2030s (capacity_ref_year approximated as 2030). Sources: electrive (2025-02-14), Electric & Hybrid Vehicle Technology International, Somerset County Council, Millbank/WEAF trade press (2026), etn.news.

Battery cell gigafactory near Šurany, Slovakia, built by the Gotion InoBat Batteries (GIB) EnergyX Slovakia joint venture — Gotion High-Tech holds ~80% and InoBat Auto ~20%. Total investment up to EUR 1.234bn on a ~65 ha (some sources cite ~95 ha) site. Construction began end of October 2025 (status: under_construction). Phase 1 nameplate = 20 GWh/yr LFP lithium-ion cells; multiple sources cite potential expansion to 40 GWh and up to 60 GWh at full build-out (kept nameplate at the firm phase-1 figure of 20 GWh; expansion not yet committed). Trial/test production targeted for 2026, full serial production expected 2027 (start_year=2027). LFP technology licensed from Gotion; output to be exported primarily to the EU (EV end market). Coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Confidence 0.85 — capacity/status/chemistry corroborated across electrive, Battery-News, CnEVPost, Rho Motion and InoBat's own newsroom; exact ramp profile and coordinates unsourced.

InoBat's planned second gigafactory ("Project Lion") at Ćuprija, Serbia. Announced Nov 2022; MOU with Serbia's Ministry of Finance and Municipality of Ćuprija signed / location selected Sep-Oct 2023; EUR 419m state incentive package confirmed Jan 2024 (total investment reported at EUR 2.3bn, 2,100+ jobs). Full nameplate reported as up to 32 GWh/year, with an initial first phase of 4 GWh originally targeted to open in 2025. Site combines EV battery + energy-storage (ESS) manufacturing with battery recycling, hence end_market = mixed. InoBat is a genuine cell manufacturer (its first Slovak Voderady/Voderady gigafactory and Novi Sad-area/Voderady lines produce high-nickel NMC/NCA Li-ion cells), so is_cell_manufacturer set true; however, several reports describe the Serbia site ambiguously as 'assembling' EV/ESS batteries plus recycling, so cell-manufacturing scope at this specific site is not 100% confirmed. Chemistry not stated for this plant (InoBat's core tech is custom high-nickel NMC/NCA; also pursuing sodium-ion) — left null. Status kept as 'announced': no confirmed groundbreaking/construction reported as of mid-2026, and the 2025 opening target appears to have slipped; backer Rio Tinto's related Serbian Jadar lithium project was reported on hold in Nov 2025, adding uncertainty. Investors/backers include Rio Tinto, Gotion and IFC — this is InoBat's own project rather than a plant-level JV, so jv_partners left null. Exact site coordinates not sourced (Ćuprija town is ~43.93N, 21.37E) — coordinates left null to avoid inventing a plant location. capacity_ref_year for the 32 GWh full nameplate not specified in sources.

Siro is a joint venture between Turkish EV maker Togg and Chinese battery maker Farasis Energy, located in Gemlik, Bursa, Turkey (adjacent to Togg's vehicle plant). Foundation stone for the battery campus laid 24 April 2023; module and pack series production began 31 March 2023 initially at ~3 GWh/yr, using imported/Farasis lithium-ion cells until in-house cell production begins. In-house battery CELL manufacturing (pouch, lithium-ion NMC) was scheduled to become operational in 2026 across a 60-hectare site; as of the latest sourced reporting this cell line was not yet confirmed as operational, hence status set to under_construction. Full nameplate cell capacity target is 20 GWh/yr, with sources giving 2031 as the year for the full 20 GWh (some earlier reports said 20 GWh by 2026 as cell production begins — figures conflict, so capacity_ref_year set to 2031 and no phased JSON recorded). End market is mixed: EV cells for Togg plus Farasis Energy Europe customers, industrial applications and stationary storage. Coordinates left null (not confirmed by a precise source). Sources: Green Car Congress (2023-04-26), Farasis Energy press releases, electrive.com. Confidence 0.7 due to capacity-year and current-status ambiguity.

Agratas is the global battery business of the Tata Group; Sanand (Gujarat, India) plant confirmed as a lithium-ion battery CELL manufacturing gigafactory (not just pack assembly). Site covers ~320 acres in Sanand GIDC. First-phase nameplate capacity 20 GWh/year, initial investment ~Rs 13,000 crore, MoU with Gujarat government signed 2023, construction began 2024. As of Dec 2025/Apr 2026 the plant is under construction with the main steel structure complete (700m x 150m, ~105,000 sqm); cell production slated to begin in 2027. Cells intended for EVs (Tata Motors) and energy storage applications, hence end_market = mixed. Chemistry (LFP vs NMC) and cell format not confirmed by a reliable source, left null. Precise coordinates not sourced (Sanand GIDC industrial area, near Ahmedabad), left null to avoid guessing. Not a JV — wholly owned by Tata/Agratas. Corroborated by ESS-News, pv magazine India/International, Battery-Tech Network, The Battery Magazine, Business Standard.

Ola Cell Technologies is the cell-manufacturing subsidiary of Ola Electric Mobility. The Gigafactory sits adjacent to Ola's Futurefactory in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu (~110 acres). It manufactures indigenous 4680-format cylindrical NMC lithium-ion cells branded "Bharat Cell." Confirmed cell manufacturer (not just pack assembly). Status: operational but at early ramp. As of early 2026, commissioned/operational cell capacity is ~1.4 GWh; cells were commercialised in vehicles from late 2025 and in the Ola Shakti home ESS launched Jan 2026 (hence end_market mixed: EV + ESS). Original commercial-production deadlines (Feb 2024, then Apr-Jun 2025) were missed; IFCI/PLI milestone letters issued in early 2025. Phase I nameplate is 5 GWh; Ola holds a 20 GWh PLI-ACC award (used as nameplate_capacity_gwh, ref 2026) and has stated ambition to scale to 100 GWh long-term (aspirational, not built). ICRA (2025) cited ~2.5 GWh operational and a 5.9 GWh calibrated phase targeted for full commercial ops by Sept 2026 — figures conflict across sources, so capacity_by_year_json kept to the confirmed ~1.4 GWh operational. Coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Sources: olaelectric.com/gigafactory; ICRA rating rationale; Business Standard (2024-06-30); electrive (2024-12-06); ess-news (2026-01-12); ANI/BioEnergy Times (2026-01-12).

Dedicated lithium-ion battery CELL gigafactory built by Exide Energy Solutions Ltd (EESL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Exide Industries Limited. Located at Phase II, Hi-Tech Defence & Aerospace Park, Polanahalli, Devanahalli, Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka, on ~80 acres leased from KIADB. Total planned nameplate 12 GWh/yr in two phases; Phase 1 is 6 GWh/yr (Phase 1 investment ~Rs 5,000 crore including pack/module lines). Cell technology licensed via a long-term technical partnership with China's SVOLT Energy Technology (technology licensing, NOT an equity JV, hence jv_partners left null). Produces both NMC cells (for higher-performance EVs) and LFP cells (for telecom, BESS, e-3W/mass-market EVs), in cylindrical and prismatic formats. Status as of July 2026: still ramping toward commercial production, not yet fully operational — first customer samples were dispatched in Q1 FY27 (Apr–Jun 2026) and commercial supplies/revenue are guided to begin Q3 FY27 (Oct–Dec 2026); earlier target had been FY26-end. Classified under_construction/commissioning on that basis; a case could be made for operational once commercial output starts later in 2026. capacity_by_year shows Phase 1 6 GWh reaching production ~2026; the eventual 12 GWh (Phase 2) timeline is not clearly dated, so capacity_ref_year left null and full nameplate recorded as 12. Exact GPS coordinates not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null (site is in the Devanahalli aerospace park area north of Bengaluru). Announced_year left null as the exact first-announcement year was not cleanly sourced (plans and land procurement reported ~2022–2023). Sources: Autocar Professional, Mercom India, SaurEnergy, EV Mechanica, Machine Maker — multiple reputable Indian trade outlets corroborate capacity, phasing and status.

jv_partners: Gotion-InoBat-Batteries (GIB, LFP tech licence), Jiangsu Highstar (NMC tech)
research_notes: Amara Raja Giga Corridor at Divitipally, Mahabubnagar district, Telangana, India; 260-acre site, INR 9,500 crore investment planned through 2031. Overall plan: up to 16 GWh lithium-ion CELL manufacturing plus ~5 GWh battery pack assembly. Operator is Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies (ARACT), a wholly owned subsidiary of Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (not a JV — technology is licensed from partners, hence they are listed as tech partners not equity JV partners). Cell tech: LFP licensed from Gotion-InoBat-Batteries / GIB EnergyX Slovakia (Gotion High-Tech), NMC tech from Jiangsu Highstar; both prismatic and cylindrical formats. Status as of July 2026: a 60 MWh Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) producing cylindrical and prismatic cells was commissioned/operational (July 2026), and a Phase-1 battery PACK assembly line (~1.5 GWh) is operational — but the main 16 GWh CELL gigafactory is still under construction, hence status=under_construction. Sources conflict slightly on the ramp: EVreporter (investor presentation) cites first phase ~4 GWh cylindrical cells in Q2/Q3 FY27; SolarQuarter cites large-scale bulk cell production of 2 GWh by June 2027. Full 16 GWh nameplate targeted by ~2031. Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null. announced_year (2023, foundation stone at Divitipally) is approximate. Additional sources: https://evreporter.com/amara-raja-collaborates-with-gotion-inobat-batteries-gib-to-license-technology-for-prismatic-and-cylindrical-cells/ ; https://www.amararaja.com/press_release/amara-raja-inaugurates-battery-pack-assembly-plant-and-lays-foundation-stone-for-customer-qualification-plant-at-its-giga-corridor/

plant_name: Reliance Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex Battery Gigafactory
research_notes: Battery gigafactory located within Reliance's Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex, Jamnagar, Gujarat, India (part of Reliance's New Energy business under RIL). Integrated cell-to-containerised-ESS operation - genuine battery CELL manufacturing, not just pack assembly. First phase of 40 GWh/year on track for commissioning in 2026 (as of June 2026 AGM all equipment delivered to site); company has committed to scale up to a 120 GWh/year target, so nameplate_capacity_gwh=120 is the eventual/full nameplate. No firm year confirmed for the 120 GWh full nameplate, so capacity_ref_year left null; capacity_by_year_json records the confirmed first-phase 40 GWh in 2026. Status = under_construction (first phase not yet producing as of July 2026). Chemistry primarily LFP (drawing on RIL subsidiaries Lithium Werks and Faradion); sodium-ion cell production being industrialised in parallel. Primarily targeted at BESS/stationary storage (ESS). Exact site coordinates not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null (complex is on ~5,000 acres near Jamnagar). announced_year ~2021 (RIL New Energy business / giga complex announced at June 2021 AGM). Cross-checked across pv magazine India, ess-news, Business Today AGM coverage. Earlier 2025 reports cited 40 GWh initial scaling to 100 GWh; June 2026 AGM updated the target to 120 GWh.

operator: ACC Energy Storage Pvt Ltd (Rajesh Exports)
research_notes: Planned 5 GWh/yr lithium-ion cell gigafactory at Dharwad, Karnataka. Rajesh Exports Ltd was one of three winners of India's INR 18,100 crore PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cells (2022 allotment: 20 GWh Ola Electric, 5 GWh Reliance New Energy, 5 GWh Rajesh Exports). Tripartite agreement (Centre + Karnataka + REL) signed Jan 2023; a wholly-owned subsidiary, ACC Energy Storage Pvt Ltd, was incorporated to execute the project. STATUS: announced only — never advanced beyond land acquisition. As of Oct 2025 the company was still struggling with land acquisition, and by June 2026 the Ministry of Heavy Industries was deciding whether to remove Rajesh Exports from the PLI scheme after a SEBI interim order alleged large-scale financial fraud (inflated revenues). No construction or production has begun; project viability is in serious doubt. Chemistry given only as "lithium-ion" (advanced chemistry cell); no cell format confirmed. End market cited as EV batteries. No site coordinates published beyond Dharwad district. Capacity 5 GWh is the eventual PLI-committed nameplate, not a phased figure. Confidence lowered because the plant may never be built. Sources: pv-magazine India (2023-01-24), Mercom India (Jan 2023), Business Standard (2026-06-07 removal decision; 2025-05-14 extension request; 2025-12-01 rule relaxation).

Commercial Li-ion cell manufacturing line at Log9's campus in Jakkur, Bengaluru, inaugurated 21 April 2023 and billed as India's first commercial Li-ion cell facility. Initial nameplate 50 MWh/year (0.05 GWh) producing large-format cylindrical cells (22-series to 66-series) in LTO and LFP chemistries for EV and industrial/ESS use (hence end_market=mixed). Company publicised plans to scale this site to ~1 GWh (with 2 GWh pack capacity) within 15-18 months, plus a separate larger gigafactory ambition (5 GWh by 2027, 25 GWh by ~2030); nameplate here kept at the confirmed built 0.05 GWh as the larger figures were unbuilt targets. Status recorded as operational (line was commissioned and running from 2023), but Log9 Materials entered NCLT insolvency in 2025 amid a cash crunch and collapsing Chinese LFP prices that undercut its LTO bet; headcount fell below 50 and a near-shutdown was reported, so current operating status of the line is uncertain - hence moderate confidence. Precise site coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. Sources: pv-magazine India (2023-04-24), thenewsminute, etn.news, saurenergy, inc42 (insolvency, 2025).

International Battery Company (IBC) is a US-founded (Silicon Valley R&D) battery cell maker building proprietary large-format I-NMC (NMC-622) prismatic Li-ion cells for EV/mobility, positioned as a non-China / FEOC-compliant supply chain. It signed an MoU with the Karnataka government in August 2023 for ~100 acres near Bengaluru airport (KIADB plot in the Information Technology Investment Region) to build a non-captive gigafactory. In Feb 2024 it raised USD 35M (Pre-Series A, led by RTP Global) to advance an initial 2 GWh line, with a stated vision of 10 GWh by 2028. In January 2025 a Rs 390 crore (~USD 45M) Bengaluru facility was announced (in collaboration with Mahanagar Gas Ltd), targeting production start within ~9 months (~late 2025) and ~300 direct jobs. Nameplate figure of 10 GWh is the eventual 2028 target; 2 GWh is the initial phase (capacity_by_year_json reflects the phased ramp). Status set to under_construction: as of latest sourcing the plant was in build/pre-production; no independent confirmation of full operation found as of mid-2026 (note: a separate ~50 MWh line, likely the South Korea pilot, is already shipping UN-certified prismatic NMC cells). Precise site coordinates not sourced (left null). Capacity/status cross-checked across PR Newswire, Pulse2, ETN News, Power Technology and Deccan Herald; exact production-start date and current operational status remain uncertain, hence moderate confidence.

operator: Amperex Technology Limited (ATL India Technology Pvt Ltd)
research_notes:
Site: IMT Sohna (Sector-20, Block C-Indri), Nuh district, Haryana, India, near Gurugram. Wholly within TDK group via subsidiary ATL (Amperex Technology Limited); Indian entity is ATL India Technology Pvt Ltd — NOT a JV, so jv_partners left null. Land: 180 acres acquired ~2020 for ~Rs 550 crore; total planned investment ~Rs 7,083 crore over six years (initial phase >Rs 3,000 crore). First phase inaugurated 4 Sep 2025 by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw; small-scale output slated to begin Q4 2025 and ramp gradually — hence status recorded as operational (early ramp) as of the 2026-07-19 access date, though full nameplate is years out.

is_cell_manufacturer = true: Reuters (Apr 2024, via investing.com/newprojectstracker) reported TDK/ATL will MANUFACTURE Li-ion battery cells in India (including iPhone cells), with cells then supplied to Apple's pack assembler Sunwoda Electronics — indicating this is a cell-fab site, not merely pack assembly. NOTE the ambiguity: much inauguration press describes output as '200 million battery PACKS/year' and '220 million pieces/year', consumer-electronics scale (phones, laptops, wearables/hearables incl. AirPods, earbuds, watches). Some early plans also mentioned 2/3-wheeler EV cells.

CAPACITY: reported only in units (200M packs or 220M pieces per year at full scale), NOT in GWh. No sourced GWh figure exists, so nameplate_capacity_gwh, capacity_ref_year and capacity_by_year_json are left null per no-invention rule (a rough back-of-envelope on ~200M small consumer cells would be single-digit GWh/yr but is unsourced). chemistry generically 'lithium-ion'; LCO/NMC and pouch cell_format are strong inferences for phone/wearable cells but not explicitly stated in sources. Coordinates not sourced to the exact plot (IMT Sohna approx 28.24N, 77.07E) so lat/long left null. Confidence 0.6 reflects solid identity/status but cell-vs-pack ambiguity and absence of a GWh capacity figure.

Sources: Reuters via investing.com (cell manufacturing, Apr 2024); newprojectstracker (Lithium-Ion Battery Cell Mfg Unit, Nuh, Rs 70,830M); indbiz.gov.in and electronicsforyou.biz (180 acres, Rs 550 cr); swarajyamag/particle.news/ddnews (Sep 2025 inauguration, 200M packs/yr, >5,000 jobs); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATL_(company).

jv_partners: Not finalised; LG Energy Solution was in JV talks (Dec 2024); partner still being scouted as of June 2026
research_notes:
Announced-stage Li-ion battery CELL manufacturing plan by JSW (JSW Group, via JSW Energy / JSW Neo Energy / JSW Green Mobility). Sources are fluid and figures conflict across three overlapping storylines:
(1) Feb 2024 Odisha MoU (Rs 40,000 crore integrated EV + battery complex at Naraj, Cuttack, plus lithium refinery/copper smelter at Paradip): a 50 GWh EV battery plant, phased from ~10 GWh by 2026 up to 50 GWh by 2028-2030 (Manufacturing Today India; ETN News).
(2) Dec 2024: JSW Energy in talks with LG Energy Solution for a ~$1.5bn, 50:50 JV, initial combined capacity 10 GWh for EV + renewable storage, targeted operational by end-2026; LGES to provide technology/equipment (EnergyTrend, Business Standard, just-auto). Deal not confirmed closed.
(3) June 2026 (most recent, cited as primary source): JSW has 'finalised' a 30 GWh Li-ion CELL plant with a JV partner, >$1.3bn, built in two phases (10 GWh, then +20 GWh for ~$600m). Chemistry stated as lithium iron phosphate (LFP), chosen for cost and India's warm climate. Partner still being scouted; one option floated is siting the plant in a Southeast Asian country. Interim cells imported from China; first NEVs targeted end-Dec 2026/early Jan 2027 (Business Standard).
nameplate set to 30 GWh (the most specific, most recent 'cell plant' figure); broader group ambition is 50 GWh. capacity_ref_year and start_year left null due to conflicting/undated phase targets. Location most likely Naraj, Cuttack, Odisha, but the cell-plant site is explicitly unsettled (SE Asia option mentioned), so coordinates left null. End market mixed (EV via JSW Green Mobility NEVs + ESS via JSW BSS/LG storage share). NOTE: separate JSW facilities exist that are NOT cell plants and were excluded — a 5 GWh battery PACK/ASSEMBLY unit in Pune and 1 GWh BESS construction. is_cell_manufacturer=true because the finalised 30 GWh plan is explicitly a Li-ion cell plant. Low confidence (0.4) due to unconfirmed partner, unconfirmed final capacity, and unconfirmed site.

GODI India announced a 12.5 GWh lithium-ion (NMC) and sodium-ion cell manufacturing gigafactory in Telangana via an MoU signed at the World Economic Forum, Davos, January 2024. research_notes: Site in Taiwa-cho, Kurokawa District, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan, operated by Toyota Battery Co., Ltd. (Primearth EV Energy / PEVE was renamed TOYOTA BATTERY Co., Ltd. on 1 Oct 2024; became a wholly-owned Toyota Motor subsidiary in March 2024 — no longer a Panasonic JV, hence jv_partners null). PEVE is a genuine cell manufacturer, producing prismatic NiMH and Li-ion cells (not just pack assembly). The Miyagi site hosts multiple facilities: three NiMH plants opened 2010–2015 (~1.4M packs/yr) plus two new Li-ion plants launched ~2019–2021 (~200,000 Li-ion HEV packs/yr). Primarily HEV automotive batteries, expanding toward PHEV/BEV. No GWh nameplate figure is published for this site — capacity is reported only in pack units, and HEV packs are sub-1 kWh, so a GWh conversion would be a guess; nameplate_capacity_gwh left null per no-invention rule. Coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. status operational. Sources: Wikipedia (Primearth EV Energy); Toyota Global Newsroom (PEVE-to-Toyota Battery rename, 2024); Obayashi Corporation project page (Miyagi 6th/7th factory); EnergyTrend (Li-ion plant expansion 2018).

AESC's original/legacy battery cell manufacturing site, located at Nissan's Zama operations complex in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan. It is a genuine cell manufacturer: trial production began mid-2009 and it produced the laminated (pouch) lithium-ion cells for the first mass-market Nissan Leaf from 2010. Cathode chemistry started as lithium manganese oxide (LMO) and later migrated to nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC, incl. high-nickel variants). Originally a Nissan-NEC joint venture (formed ~2007); Envision Group (China) acquired a controlling stake in 2018-2019, making it Envision AESC, so it is no longer treated as a live JV (single operator AESC, parent Envision Group). The site remains operational as part of AESC's global network. Nameplate capacity of ~2.6 GWh/yr comes from secondary capacity trackers rather than a primary company disclosure, hence moderate confidence and capacity_ref_year set approximately to 2024. End market is EV (Nissan). Exact plant coordinates were not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null rather than guessed. announced_year (2007) reflects the JV formation; start_year (2010) reflects first Leaf-cell production (trial line 2009).

Announced Nov 2023: a ~C$1.05bn ("$1 billion") gigafactory to redevelop E-One Moli's existing 1990-built site at 20000 Stewart Crescent, Maple Ridge, British Columbia into Canada's largest high-performance lithium-ion battery cell plant. Rated capacity ~2.8 GWh/yr, equal to up to 135 million cylindrical (21700-class) high-power NMC cells per year (chemistry: Molicel uses NMC 622/532 in 21700 format). End markets are diverse/mixed: automotive/EV, aerospace, power tools, consumer electronics, garden equipment and medical devices — not a mass-EV plant. Government support pledged: up to C$204.5m federal (Strategic Innovation Fund / Net Zero Accelerator) + C$80m provincial. Construction was to begin ~June 2024 with operations targeted for 2028.

STATUS CAVEAT: In December 2024, parent Taiwan Cement Corp. (chairman Nelson Chang) confirmed the expansion/construction was halted/paused, citing difficulty expanding overseas before Taiwanese plants run at full scale; Canada confirmed no government money had been spent. The status enum lacks a "cancelled/on-hold" value; recorded as "announced" because the gigafactory never reached operational status and construction was stopped before meaningful build-out. Note: E-One Moli has operated an R&D/limited manufacturing presence in Maple Ridge since 1990, but the large-scale cell plant here is the announced (now stalled) project. nameplate 2.8 GWh and 2028 start are planned/nameplate figures now uncertain due to the halt. Coordinates left null (site address 20000 Stewart Crescent, Maple Ridge BC known, but precise decimal coords not independently sourced). Capacity figure (2.8 GWh / 135m cells) corroborated across Electric Autonomy, SustainableBiz and government releases; status halt reported by Electric Autonomy and Business in Vancouver (Dec 2024).
